mechanism.name: Repeated-cross-sectional instrumented DiD with bridge confounding

generation_equations.label: baseline repeated cross-section
generation_equations.expression: X1,X2 iid N(0,1); Z,T iid Bernoulli(0.5); U0,U1 iid bridge(phi=0.5), density f(u)=1/[2*pi*cosh(u/2)]. Baseline/exogenous draws independent across rows and variables. U=2*log(tan(pi*V/2)), V Uniform(0,1); exact machine endpoint0 is redrawn.

generation_equations.label: period outcomes
generation_equations.expression: s(X)=1.5X1+2X2-0.5; Y0=200+10*[A0*s(X)+0.5U0+2Z+1.5X1+2X2]+e0; Y1=240+10*[A1*s(X)+0.5U1+2Z+2X1+1.5X2]+e1; e0,e1 iid N(0,1), independent of all other primitive draws.

generation_equations.label: observation and sample-size interface
generation_equations.expression: A=(1-T)*A0+T*A1; Y=(1-T)*Y0+T*Y1; return X1,X2,Z,T,A,Y only. n is total individuals; paper baseline n=5000 independently tested; official n=32 smoke is a sample-size extension due to unmodified tool cap2048, not an official n5000 pass.

generation_equations.label: population causal target
generation_equations.expression: tau_t(x)=E[Y_t(1)-Y_t(0)|X=x]=10*s(x); ATE=E[tau_t(X)]=-5. This is not ATT, finite-sample SATT, PCD or a policy-performance estimand.

sampling.unit: One independent cross-sectional individual observed at exactly one time T in{0,1}. External n is total row count, not n per period and not a paired panel.
sampling.dependence: Rows iid; independent X1,X2 standard normals; independent U0,U1 bridge(phi=.5); independent Z,T Bernoulli(.5); conditionally independent treatment draws and N(0,1) outcome errors. No serial initialization, common factors or donor construction.

assumptions: Source instrumented-DiD consistency/random sampling, random Z and T, no instrument effect on the untreated trend, stable CATE and no shared unmeasured effect modifier.

All normal/bridge/Bernoulli innovations are independent as in author simulation/main.R; treatment depends on latent U and observed X, so ordinary unconfoundedness and ordinary unconditional parallel trends are not asserted.
The scalar truth uses specified intervention conditional means and the standard-normal population, not a finite sample average of heterogenous individual effects.

properties.notes: Two baseline Gaussian covariates; observed binary IV Z and observation-period T have separate schema roles. Treatment logit depends on latent bridge confounding; response has A-by-X interactions. No latent bridge values are observed.

estimand.name: ATE
estimand.definition: Population average causal effect E[Y_t(1)-Y_t(0)]=E[10(1.5X1+2X2-0.5)]=-5 for either t=0 or1, over X~N(0,I2), and original natural Z,U. Not ATT, a finite-sample SATT, optimal-policy value or PCD.

truth.expression: Population average causal effect E[Y_t(1)-Y_t(0)]=E[10(1.5X1+2X2-0.5)]=-5 for either t=0 or1, over X~N(0,I2), and original natural Z,U. Not ATT, a finite-sample SATT, optimal-policy value or PCD.
truth.derivation: Conditional intervention mean difference is15X1+20X2-5; independent zero-mean normal population gives ATE=-5 exactly. Independent verify uses rational polynomial coefficient subtraction and normal symmetry.

adaptations: Preserve the complete Section6 main-simulation distribution. Python local random.Random replaces R RNG; no claim of stream or estimator-performance reproduction.
Choose scalar population ATE E[tau(X)]=-5, the Section4 underlying estimand, rather than learning a policy or reporting PCD; it is not ATT.
External n counts independent repeated-cross-sectional rows; n=5000 is the main parametric-model source baseline. Other n are interface sample-size extensions; sample-size changes remain one family.
Only observed X1,X2,Z,T,A,Y are returned. No coupled potential outcomes or latent variables are exported; only the source-observed law and conditional mean causal effect are needed.
